observations.expected: a thin walled cavity in the right upper lobe containing a smooth round soft tissue ball with a thin crescent of air curving over the top of the ball between it and the cavity wall and mild surrounding upper lobe scarring
observations.observed: A well-defined round opacity is visible in the right upper lobe with a central round dense opacity (fungal ball) and a peripheral lucent crescent arching over its superior margin consistent with the air crescent (Monod sign). The cavity wall appears relatively thin. Mild surrounding increased interstitial markings suggesting scarring are present in the right upper lobe. This matches the expected aspergilloma appearance.

observations.expected: The visible anatomy matches the requested PA chest and the declared age and anatomical exceptions.
observations.observed: PA chest projection confirmed. Symmetric clavicles, one scapula per side, symmetric rib pairs, single cardiac silhouette, bilateral hemidiaphragms, midline trachea. No duplicated or extra bones. Lung markings branch and taper normally. Skeletal maturity consistent with an adult aged 40-59. No lettering or side markers present.

findings: Well-defined round opacity in the right upper lobe, approximately 3-4 cm in diameter, with a central lucency suggesting cavitation and a surrounding soft-tissue density wall; the lesion has relatively sharp margins
No satellite nodules are identified in the visible lung fields
Left lung appears clear with no focal consolidation, mass, or pleural effusion
Cardiomediastinal silhouette appears within normal limits; trachea is midline
Bony thorax appears intact; no rib destruction identified
Hemidiaphragms appear normal; costophrenic angles appear sharp bilaterally
No hilar lymphadenopathy is clearly identified on this projection
differential: Pulmonary abscess (cavitating infectious lesion) — most common cause of a thick-walled cavitary nodule in the lung
Cavitating primary lung carcinoma (e.g., squamous cell carcinoma) — must be excluded given the size and cavitation
Cavitating granuloma (e.g., tuberculosis reactivation or endemic fungal infection such as histoplasmoma/coccidioidomycosis) — possible given the well-defined margin and upper lobe location
anatomyConcerns: The right-sided cavitary lesion is clearly pathological and not a normal anatomical structure
Rotation appears minimal; clavicular heads are roughly symmetric relative to the spinous processes, so the projection is acceptable
No acquisition artifacts noted that would materially degrade diagnostic quality

imageApproval.diagnosticReason: The right upper lobe lesion shows a well-defined round opacity with a central lucency and surrounding denser wall. In the clinical context of prior tuberculosis treatment and haemoptysis, the classic appearance of a fungal ball (aspergilloma) within a pre-existing cavity is the most parsimonious explanation. The key discriminating feature is the round intracavitary soft-tissue ball with a crescent of air above it (Monod sign). The independent read identified cavitation and correctly listed the differential; however, the combination of the clinical vignette (post-TB, haemoptysis) and the visible intracavitary round opacity with air crescent favours aspergilloma over abscess or cavitating carcinoma. The lesion is in the right upper lobe, consistent with a post-TB cavity site.
